whatItIs.text: Rice with only the husk removed, keeping the bran and germ — chewier, nuttier, and slower to cook than white rice, with more of the grain intact.

historyNote.text: Rice was domesticated in China some 13,500-8,200 years ago and independently in West Africa about 3,000 years ago; brown rice is simply the less-milled form of the same grain — 'dry rice grain is milled to remove the outer layers', and how much is removed gives white or brown.

howToChoose.text: Look for even, unbroken grains with a faint nutty smell; the bran means a shorter shelf life than white rice, so buy in smaller bags if you cook it rarely.

storage.text: Keep dry in a sealed container in a cool cupboard.

useItUp.text: Cooked brown rice grains stay distinct in fried rice and grain bowls, and it makes a fine porridge with stock and a soft egg.
